items.informal_name: Multiplication by Non-Zero Rational Preserves LiouvilleWith Property
items.type: ∀ {p x : ℝ} {r : ℚ}, r ≠ 0 → (LiouvilleWith p (x * ↑r) ↔ LiouvilleWith p x)
items.informal_description: For any non-zero rational number $ r $, a real number $ x $ is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ if and only if $ x \cdot r $ is also a Liouville number with exponent $ p $.

items.informal_name: Liouville numbers with a given exponent are closed under multiplication by non-zero rationals
items.type: ∀ {p x : ℝ} {r : ℚ}, LiouvilleWith p x → r ≠ 0 → LiouvilleWith p (↑r * x)
items.informal_description: If $x$ is a Liouville number with exponent $p$, and $r$ is a non-zero rational number, then the product $r \cdot x$ is also a Liouville number with exponent $p$.

items.informal_name: Multiplication by Non-Zero Rational Preserves Liouville Property with Exponent p
items.type: ∀ {p x : ℝ} {r : ℚ}, LiouvilleWith p x → r ≠ 0 → LiouvilleWith p (x * ↑r)
items.informal_description: For any real number $ x $ that is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ and any non-zero rational number $ r $, the product $ x \cdot r $ is also a Liouville number with exponent $ p $.

items.informal_name: Multiplication by Non-Zero Rational Preserves Liouville Property with Exponent p
items.type: ∀ {p x : ℝ} {r : ℚ}, r ≠ 0 → (LiouvilleWith p (↑r * x) ↔ LiouvilleWith p x)
items.informal_description: For any non-zero rational number $ r $, a real number $ x $ is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ if and only if the product $ r \cdot x $ is also a Liouville number with exponent $ p $. This equivalence holds because multiplying by a non-zero rational scalar preserves the approximation properties defining Liouville numbers.

items.informal_name: Multiplication by Non-Zero Natural Number Preserves LiouvilleWith Property
items.type: ∀ {p x : ℝ} {n : ℕ}, n ≠ 0 → (LiouvilleWith p (x * ↑n) ↔ LiouvilleWith p x)
items.informal_description: For any non-zero natural number $ n $ and real number $ x $, the product $ x \cdot n $ is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ if and only if $ x $ is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $.

items.informal_name: Multiplication by Non-Zero Integers Preserves Liouville Property with Exponent p
items.type: ∀ {p x : ℝ} {m : ℤ}, m ≠ 0 → (LiouvilleWith p (x * ↑m) ↔ LiouvilleWith p x)
items.informal_description: For any non-zero integer $ m $ and real number $ x $, $ x $ is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ if and only if $ x \cdot m $ is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $. This equivalence holds because scaling by a non-zero integer does not affect the approximation properties defining Liouville numbers.

items.informal_name: Multiplication by Non-Zero Integer Preserves Liouville Property with Exponent $ p $
items.type: ∀ {p x : ℝ} {m : ℤ}, LiouvilleWith p x → m ≠ 0 → LiouvilleWith p (x * ↑m)
items.informal_description: If $ x $ is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ and $ m $ is a non-zero integer, then the product $ x \cdot m $ is also a Liouville number with the same exponent $ p $. This means that for any positive constant $ C $, there exist infinitely many rational numbers $ \frac{a}{n} $ such that $ |x \cdot m - \frac{a}{n}| < \frac{C}{n^p} $.

items.informal_name: Multiplication by Non-Zero Natural Number Preserves Liouville Property with Exponent p
items.type: ∀ {p x : ℝ} {n : ℕ}, n ≠ 0 → (LiouvilleWith p (↑n * x) ↔ LiouvilleWith p x)
items.informal_description: For any non-zero natural number $ n $ and real number $ x $, the real number $ x $ is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $ if and only if the product $ n \cdot x $ is a Liouville number with exponent $ p $. This equivalence holds because multiplying by a non-zero natural number does not affect the approximation properties defining Liouville numbers.
